Synopsis:
South Sudan's Dar Blend heavy-sweet crude is returning to Singapore/Malaysia marine fuel blending pools in August 2026, after a period of diversion to Chinese refineries (March–July) triggered by Middle East heavy crude disruptions from the U.S.-Iran war. With China's incremental crude options expanding, demand for Dar Blend has eased, sending ~1.7M barrels back into the bunker blending pool. This is pressuring Singapore 0.5% low-sulphur fuel oil (LSFO) spot differentials to monthly lows, though tight cutter/blendstock availability is seen limiting further downside.
